title.zh: 卷十四 梁書14: 列傳第四 羅紹威 趙犨 王珂
title.en: Volume 14 Book of Later Liang 14: Biographies 4 - Luo Shaowei, Zhao Chou, Wang Ke
title.raw: 卷十四 梁書14: 列傳第四 羅紹威 趙犨 王珂 Volume 14 Book of Later Liang 14: Biographies 4 - Luo Shaowei, Zhao Chou, Wang Ke

sentences.zh: 羅紹威，

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei,
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Shaowei's style name:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Shaowei's style name:

sentences.zh: （《舊唐書》云：紹威，字端己。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 says: Shaowei, style name Duanji.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 gives his style as Duanji.)〉

sentences.zh: 魏州貴鄉人。

translations.literal: was a native of Guixiang in Wei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: came from Guixiang in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 父宏信，本名宗弁，初為馬牧監，事節度使樂彥貞。

translations.literal: His father Hongxin, original name Zongbian, at first was horse-pasture inspector and served military commissioner Le Yanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongxin, born Zongbian, began as a horse-pasture inspector under Commissioner Le Yanzhen.

sentences.zh: 光啟末，彥貞子從訓驕盈太橫，招聚兵甲，欲誅牙軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Yanzhen's son Congxun was insolent and overbearing, gathered armor and weapons, and wished to execute the guard army.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Guangqi, Yanzhen's son Congxun grew arrogant, armed his followers, and plotted to wipe out the guard.

sentences.zh: 牙軍怒，聚噪攻之，從訓出據相州。

translations.literal: The guard army in anger gathered and clamored to attack him; Congxun went out and held Xiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The guards rose in fury; Congxun fled and seized Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 牙軍廢彥貞，囚於龍興寺，逼令為僧，尋殺之，推小校趙文建為留後。

translations.literal: The guard army deposed Yanzhen, imprisoned him at Longxing Monastery, forced him to become a monk, soon killed him, and pushed junior officer Zhao Wenjian to be acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: They deposed Yanzhen, jailed him at Longxing Monastery, made him a monk, then killed him and made junior officer Zhao Wenjian acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是，宏信自言，於所居遇一白須翁，謂之曰：「 爾當為土地主。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hongxin had said that at his dwelling he met a white-bearded old man who told him: "You shall be lord of this land."
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin once said a white-bearded elder at his home told him, "You will rule this land."

sentences.zh: 」如是者再，心竊異之。

translations.literal: Thus twice; in his heart he secretly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: It happened twice, and he took it as an omen.

sentences.zh: 既而文建不洽軍情，牙軍聚呼曰：「孰願為節度使者？

translations.literal: When Wenjian did not harmonize with the army's hearts, the guard army gathered and shouted: "Who wishes to be military commissioner?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjian lost the army's trust, the guards cried, "Who will be commissioner?"

sentences.zh: 」宏信即應曰：「白須翁早以命我，可以君長爾曹。

translations.literal: Hongxin immediately answered: "The white-bearded elder long ago gave me the mandate—you may make me your chief."
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin answered, "The white-bearded elder chose me—you may make me your leader."

sentences.zh: 」唐文德元年四月，牙軍推宏信為留後。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Wende year 1 of Tang, the guard army pushed Hongxin to be acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Wende 1, month 4, the guards made Hongxin acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，即正授節旄。

translations.literal: The court heard it and at once formally granted the command banner.
translations.idiomatic: The court confirmed him with the commission banner.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，太祖急攻兗、鄆，朱瑄求援於太原。

translations.literal: In Qianning, the Founder pressed the attack on Yan and Yanzhou; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianning the Founder besieged Yan; Zhu Xuan begged Taiyuan for help.

sentences.zh: 時李克用遣大將李存信率師赴之，假道於魏，屯於莘縣。

translations.literal: At that time Li Keyong sent the great general Li Cunxin with troops to go; borrowing the road through Wei, he camped at Xin county.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent Li Cunxin through Wei, where he camped at Xin county.

sentences.zh: 存信御軍無法，稍侵魏之芻牧，宏信不平之。

translations.literal: Cunxin commanded troops without discipline and gradually encroached on Wei's fodder and pasture; Hongxin was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin's men looted Wei fodder; Hongxin resented it.

sentences.zh: 太祖因遣使謂宏信曰：「太原誌吞河朔，回戈之日，貴道堪憂。

translations.literal: The Founder therefore sent an envoy telling Hongxin: "Taiyuan intends to swallow the lands north of the Yellow River; on the day they turn their spears back, your circuit will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder warned Hongxin, "Taiyuan means to swallow the north; when they turn homeward, Wei will be in danger."

sentences.zh: 」宏信懼，乃歸款於太祖，仍出師三萬攻李存信，敗之。

translations.literal: Hongxin in fear then submitted to the Founder, still marched out thirty thousand to attack Li Cunxin, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Taiyuan, Hongxin submitted and sent thirty thousand men who routed Cunxin.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李克用領兵攻魏，營於觀音門外，屬邑多拔。

translations.literal: Before long Li Keyong led troops to attack Wei, camped outside Guanyin Gate, and many dependent prefectures were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Keyong besieged Wei at Guanyin Gate and seized nearby towns.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣葛從周援之，戰於洹水，擒克用男落落以獻。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Ge Congzhou to aid him; they fought at Huan River and captured Keyong's son Luoluo to present.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Ge Congzhou; at Huan River they captured Keyong's son Luoluo.

sentences.zh: 太祖令送於宏信，斬之，晉軍乃退。

translations.literal: The Founder had him sent to Hongxin, who beheaded him, and the Jin army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin beheaded Luoluo and the Jin army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是時，太祖方圖兗、鄆，慮宏信離貳，每歲時賂遺，必卑辭厚禮。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder was planning Yan and Yanzhou and feared Hongxin would turn aside; each year's seasonal gifts were sure to use humble words and rich courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: While attacking Yan the Founder courted Hongxin yearly with humble, lavish gifts lest Wei turn away.

sentences.zh: 宏信每有答貺，太祖必對魏使北面拜而受之，曰：「六兄比予有倍年之長，兄弟之國，安得以常鄰遇之。

translations.literal: Whenever Hongxin had return gifts, the Founder would face Wei's envoy and bow north to receive them, saying: "Sixth Brother is more than a year my elder—in a brother state, how can I be met as a common neighbor?"
translations.idiomatic: He bowed north to Wei envoys, saying, "Sixth Brother is my elder in a brotherhood—I cannot treat him as a mere neighbor."

sentences.zh: 」故宏信以為厚己。

translations.literal: Thus Hongxin thought himself deeply honored.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin believed himself honored.

sentences.zh: 其後，宏信累官至檢校太尉，封臨清王。

translations.literal: Afterward Hongxin rose in rank to honorary Grand Marshal and was enfeoffed Prince of Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to honorary Grand Marshal and Prince of Linqing.

sentences.zh: 光化元年八月，薨於位。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Guanghua year 1 he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Guanghua 1, month 8.

sentences.zh: 紹威襲父位為留後，

translations.literal: Shaowei succeeded his father as acting commissioner,
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei succeeded as acting commissioner,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Shaowei's early offices:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Shaowei's early offices:

sentences.zh: （《舊唐書》：紹威自文德初授左散騎常侍，充天雄軍節度副使，自龍紀至乾寧，十年之中，累加官爵。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Old Book of Tang》: From Wende at first Shaowei was appointed Left Regular Cavalry Attendant and deputy military commissioner of Tianxiong; from Longji to Qianning, in ten years he repeatedly received offices and titles.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 records steady promotion from Wende through Qianning.)〉

sentences.zh: 朝廷因而命之，尋正授旄鉞，累加檢校太尉、兼侍中，封長沙郡王。

translations.literal: The court thereupon ordered him, soon formally granted the axe and banner, and he was repeatedly raised to honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Palace Secretary, enfeoffed Prince of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The court confirmed him with full commission, Grand Marshal, Palace Secretary, and the title Prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 昭宗東遷，命諸道修洛邑，紹威獨營太廟，製加守侍中，進封鄴王。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong moved east, he ordered the circuits to repair Luoyang; Shaowei alone built the Great Temple, was made co-equal chief minister with the added title, and advanced to Prince of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved east, Shaowei alone rebuilt the Great Temple, became chief minister, and was made Prince of Ye.

sentences.zh: 初，至德中，田承嗣盜據相、魏、澶、博、衛、貝等六州，召募軍中子弟，置之部下，號曰「牙軍」，皆豐給厚賜，不勝驕寵。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Zhide, Tian Chengsi seized six prefectures—Xiang, Wei, Cang, Bo, Wei, and Bei—and recruited army youths into his command, called the "Guard Army," all richly fed and rewarded, unbearably pampered and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhide, Tian Chengsi had held six prefectures and pampered a "Guard Army" of soldier sons beyond all discipline.

sentences.zh: 年代浸遠，父子相襲，親黨膠固，其凶戾者，強賈豪奪，逾法犯令，長吏不能禁。

translations.literal: As years stretched on, fathers and sons succeeded one another, kin cliques bonded solid; the fierce ones forcibly sold and plundered, violated law and orders, and long officials could not forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: Generations of guards grew into kin cliques that plundered at will while officials looked on.

sentences.zh: 變易主帥，有同兒戲，自田氏已後，垂二百年。

translations.literal: Changing commanders was like child's play; from the Tian house onward, nearly two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: They swapped commanders like toys for nearly two centuries after the Tian clan.

sentences.zh: 主帥廢置，出於其手，如史憲誠、何全皞、韓君雄、樂彥貞，皆為其所立。

translations.literal: Commanders' removal and installation came from their hands—men like Shi Xianzheng, He Quanhan, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen were all set up by them.
translations.idiomatic: They installed every commander—Shi Xianzheng, He Quanhan, Han Junxiong, Le Yanzhen among them.

sentences.zh: 優獎小不如意，則舉族被誅。

translations.literal: If rewards for petty matters fell short, whole clans were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Displease them slightly and your whole clan died.

sentences.zh: 紹威懲其往弊，雖以貨賂姑息，而心銜之。

translations.literal: Shaowei took warning from past abuses; though he placated them with bribes, in his heart he resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei bribed the guards but hated the system.

sentences.zh: 紹威嗣世之明年正月，幽州劉仁恭擁兵十萬，謀亂河朔，進陷貝州，長驅攻魏。

translations.literal: In the first month of the year after Shaowei succeeded, Youzhou's Liu Rengong massed a hundred thousand troops, plotted disorder in Hebei, advanced and took Bei prefecture, and drove straight at Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In his second year, month 1, Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched a hundred thousand into Hebei, took Bei, and struck Wei.

sentences.zh: 紹威求援於太祖，太祖遣李思安援之，屯於洹水。

translations.literal: Shaowei sought aid from the Founder; the Founder sent Li Si'an to aid him, encamped at Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei begged the Founder, who sent Li Si'an to camp at Huan River.

sentences.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏州。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou led troops into Wei prefecture from Xing and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou entered Wei from Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 燕將劉守文、單可及與王師戰於內黃，大敗之，乘勝追躡。

translations.literal: Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji fought the royal army at Neihuang, were greatly defeated, and pursuit pressed on.
translations.idiomatic: Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji were crushed at Neihuang and pursued.

sentences.zh: 會從周亦出軍掩擊，又敗燕軍，斬首三萬餘級。

translations.literal: When Congzhou also came out and struck from ambush, he again defeated the Yan army and beheaded more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhou ambushed them again and took thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 三年，紹威遣使會軍，同攻滄州以報之。

translations.literal: In year 3 Shaowei sent envoys to join armies and together attack Cangzhou in return.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he joined the Founder's assault on Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 自是紹威感太祖援助之恩，深加景附。

translations.literal: From then Shaowei felt the Founder's aid and drew very close in loyal attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he clung to the Founder in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 紹威見唐祚衰陵，群雄交亂，太祖兵強天下，必知有禪代之志，故傾心附結，讚成其事，每慮牙軍變易，心不自安。

translations.literal: Shaowei saw Tang's mandate decline, heroes contend in disorder, and the Founder's troops strongest under Heaven—he must intend to usurp—and therefore bent his heart to alliance and aided the affair, yet each time feared guard mutiny and was ill at ease in his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Tang fail and the Founder's power rise, Shaowei backed his bid for the throne yet lived in fear of the guards.

sentences.zh: 天祐初，州城地無故自陷，俄而小校李公牷謀變，紹威愈懼，乃定計圖牙軍，遣使告太祖，求為外援。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou, the prefectural city ground sank without cause; soon junior officer Li Gongquan plotted mutiny; Shaowei grew more afraid, fixed a plan against the guard army, sent envoys to tell the Founder, and begged outside aid.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianyou the city sank; officer Li Gongquan plotted revolt; Shaowei planned to destroy the guards and begged the Founder's aid.

sentences.zh: 太祖許之，遣李思安會魏博軍再攻滄州。

translations.literal: The Founder agreed and sent Li Si'an to join Wei-Bo troops in again attacking Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder agreed and sent Li Si'an with Wei troops against Cangzhou again.

sentences.zh: 先是，安陽公主薨於魏，太祖因之遣長直軍校馬嗣勳選兵千人，伏兵仗於巨橐中，肩舁以入魏州，言助女葬事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Princess Anyang had died at Wei; the Founder therefore sent long-duty camp officer Ma Sixun to select a thousand men, weapons hidden in great sacks, carried on shoulders into Weizhou, saying they came to help bury his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Anyang died at Wei, the Founder sent Ma Sixun with a thousand men hidden in funeral coffers into the city.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年正月五日，太祖親率大軍濟河，聲言視行營於滄、景，牙軍頗疑其事。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of Tianyou year 3, the Founder personally led a great army across the river, announcing he would inspect camps at Cang and Jing; the guard army was quite suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 3, month 1, day 5, the Founder crossed the river claiming to inspect Cang and Jing camps; the guards grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 是月十六日，紹威率奴客數百與嗣勳同攻之，時宿於牙城者千餘人，遲明盡誅之，凡八千家，皆赤其族，州城為之一空。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth of that month Shaowei led several hundred retainers with Sixun to attack together; at that time those quartered in the guard city were a thousand-odd—by dawn all were executed, eight thousand households in all, clans wiped red; the prefectural city was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: On day 16 Shaowei and Sixun slaughtered the thousand guards and eight thousand kin until the city stood empty.

sentences.zh: 翌日，太祖自內黃馳至鄴。

translations.literal: The next day the Founder galloped from Neihuang to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the Founder rode in from Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 時魏軍二萬，方與王師同圍滄州，聞城中有變，乃擁大將史仁遇保於高唐，六州之內，皆為敵，太祖遣諸將分討之，半歲方平。

translations.literal: At that time twenty thousand Wei troops were with the royal army besieging Cangzhou; hearing of the city's turmoil, they pushed great general Shi Renyu to hold Gaotang; within the six prefectures all became enemies; the Founder sent generals to suppress them—half a year before it was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand Wei troops at Cangzhou rebelled under Shi Renyu; six prefectures turned hostile until the Founder pacified them in six months.

sentences.zh: 自是紹威雖除其逼，然尋有自弱之悔。

translations.literal: From then Shaowei though rid of their pressure yet soon had regret at self-weakening.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei ended the guard threat but soon regretted weakening himself.

sentences.zh: 不數月，復有浮陽之役，紹威飛挽饋運，自鄴至長蘆五百里，疊跡重軌，不絕於路。

translations.literal: Within months came the Fuyang campaign; Shaowei rushed transport from Ye to Changlu five hundred li, tracks doubled and overlapped without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He fed the Fuyang campaign with convoys from Ye to Changlu, five hundred li without pause.

sentences.zh: 又於魏州建元帥府署，沿道置亭候，供牲牢、酒備、軍幕、什器，上下數十萬人，一無闕者。

translations.literal: He also built a marshal's headquarters at Weizhou, set pavilions along the road, supplied victims, wine, stores, tents, and gear—tens of thousands above and below, not one thing lacking.
translations.idiomatic: He built a marshal's hall at Wei and stocked the road with every supply for tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 及太祖回自長蘆，復過魏州，紹威乘間謂太祖曰：「邠、岐、太原終有狂譎之志，各以興復唐室為詞，王宜自取神器，以絕人望。

translations.literal: When the Founder returned from Changlu and again passed Weizhou, Shaowei took occasion to tell the Founder: "Bin, Qi, and Taiyuan will in the end have wild schemes; each takes restoring Tang as its slogan—you should yourself take the sacred vessel to cut off men's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: On the Founder's return he urged him, "Bin, Qi, and Taiyuan still dream of Tang restoration—seize the throne yourself."

sentences.zh: 天與不取，古人所非。

translations.literal: Heaven's gift not taken—of this the ancients disapproved."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate unused is what the ancients condemned."

sentences.zh: 」太祖深感之。

translations.literal: The Founder was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder took it to heart.

sentences.zh: 及登極，加守太傅、兼中書令，賜號扶天啟運竭節功臣。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Shaowei was raised to Grand Tutor and concurrent Grand Secretary, granted the title Exhausting Heaven, Initiating Fortune, Utmost Loyalty Merit Minister.
translations.idiomatic: At his enthronement Shaowei became Grand Tutor and Grand Secretary with the merit title Exhausting Heaven and Initiating Fortune.

sentences.zh: 車駕將入洛，奉詔重修五鳳樓、朝元殿，巨木良匠非當時所有，倏架於地，溯流西立於舊址之上，張設綈繡，皆有副焉。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to enter Luo, by edict he rebuilt the Five Phoenix Tower and Chaoyuan Hall; great timbers and master craftsmen were not to be had then—suddenly they were raised on the ground and, going upstream, set on the old sites; hangings of silk were all doubled.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the Five Phoenix Tower and Chaoyuan Hall for the capital entry with timbers no one else could find.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚喜，以寶帶、名馬賜之。

translations.literal: The Founder was very pleased and bestowed jeweled belts and famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder rewarded him with belts and horses.

sentences.zh: 先是，河朔三鎮司管鑰、備灑掃皆有閹人，紹威曰：「此類皆宮禁指使，豈人臣家所宜畜也。

translations.literal: Earlier, the three Hebei circuits all had eunuchs for keys, guards, and sweeping—Shaowei said: "These sorts are all palace envoys—how is it fitting for a minister's house to keep them?"
translations.idiomatic: He refused to keep palace eunuchs as household stewards, saying they belonged at court alone.

sentences.zh: 」因搜獲三十餘輩，盡以來獻，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: He therefore searched out more than thirty and sent them all as tribute; the Founder praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent thirty eunuchs to the Founder, who praised him.

sentences.zh: 開平中，加守太師、兼中書令，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: In Kaiping he was raised to Grand Preceptor and concurrent Grand Secretary, fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping he became Grand Preceptor, Grand Secretary, with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 紹威嘗以臨淄、海岱罷兵歲久，儲庾山積，惟京師軍民多而食益寡，願於太行伐木，下安陽、淇門，斫船三百艘，置水運自大河入洛口，歲漕百萬石，以給宿衛，太祖深然之。

translations.literal: Shaowei once said that Linzi and the eastern sea had long known peace, granaries heaped like mountains, while the capital's soldiers and people grew many and food grew scarce; he wished to fell timber on the Taihang, float it down Anyang and Qimen, hew three hundred boats, set water transport from the great river into Luokou, and yearly move a million piculs for the palace guard—the Founder deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a Taihang timber route and river convoys of a million piculs yearly to feed the capital—the Founder agreed.

sentences.zh: 會紹威遘疾革，遣使上章乞骸骨，太祖撫案動容，顧使者曰：「亟行語而主，為我強飯，如有不可諱，當世世貴爾子孫以相報也。

translations.literal: When Shaowei fell gravely ill he sent an envoy memorializing to beg leave of office; the Founder struck the desk moved in countenance and told the envoy: "Go quickly and tell your lord to eat strongly for me; if the end cannot be avoided, I shall ennoble your sons and grandsons generation after generation in return."
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he begged to retire; the Founder wept and promised his children would be honored forever.

sentences.zh: 」仍命其子周翰監總軍府。

translations.literal: He still ordered his son Zhouhan to oversee the military government.
translations.idiomatic: He left son Zhouhan in charge of the army.

sentences.zh: 及訃至，輟朝三日，冊贈尚書令。

translations.literal: When the death report arrived, court mourning halted three days; he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourned three days and posthumously made him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 紹威在鎮凡十七年，年三十四薨。

translations.literal: Shaowei was at his post altogether seventeen years; he died at age thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled seventeen years and died at thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 紹威形貌魁偉，有英傑氣，攻筆劄，曉音律。

translations.literal: Shaowei's form was tall and imposing, with heroic air; he attacked brush writing and understood music.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and heroic, he wrote well and understood music.

sentences.zh: 性復精悍明敏，服膺儒術，明達吏理。

translations.literal: By nature he was also sharp, bright, and keen, embraced Ruist learning, and was clear in clerkly governance.
translations.idiomatic: Sharp and learned, he governed with Confucian clarity.

sentences.zh: 好招延文士，聚書萬卷，開學館，置書樓，每歌酒宴會，與賓佐賦詩，頗有情致。

translations.literal: He loved to gather literary men, collected ten thousand scrolls, opened a school hall, set up a book tower; at each song-and-wine banquet with guests and aides he composed poetry with quite emotional charm.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered scholars, ten thousand books, a school and library, and wrote poetry at every feast.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Shaowei's literary fame:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Shaowei's literary fame:

sentences.zh: （《太平廣記》引《羅紹威傳》云：當時藩牧之中，最獲文章之譽。

translations.literal: (The 《Extensive Records of the Taiping Era》 cites the 《Biography of Luo Shaowei》: Among frontier governors then he won the greatest reputation for letters.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Taiping Era》 cites his biography: among frontier lords he was most praised for writing.

sentences.zh: 每命幕客作四方書檄，小不稱意，壞裂抵棄，自擘箋起草，下筆成文，雖無藻麗之風，幕客多所不及。）〉

translations.literal: Whenever he ordered staff to draft letters to the four directions, if slightly not to his mind he tore and cast them away, himself tore paper and drafted—when the brush descended, composition was done; though without ornate flourish, staff often could not match.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He rewrote staff drafts himself and finished dispatches on the spot—often better than his aides.)〉

sentences.zh: 江東人羅隱者，佐錢鏐軍幕，有詩名於天下。

translations.literal: Jiangdong man Luo Yin aided Qian Liu's military staff and had poetic fame under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The poet Luo Yin served Qian Liu in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 紹威遣使賂遺，敘南巷之敬，隱乃聚其所為詩投寄之。

translations.literal: Shaowei sent envoys with gifts and narrated respect from the southern lane; Yin then gathered his poems and sent them.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei sent gifts; Yin sent his collected poems.

sentences.zh: 紹威酷嗜其作，因目己之所為曰《偷江東集》，至今鄴中人士諷詠之。

translations.literal: Shaowei avidly loved his work and therefore titled his own writings 《Stealing the Jiangdong Collection》; to this day Ye gentlemen chant them.
translations.idiomatic: He adored Yin's verse and named his own book 《Stealing the Jiangdong Collection》.

sentences.zh: 紹威嘗有公宴詩云：「簾前淡泊雲頭日，座上蕭騷雨腳風。

translations.literal: Shaowei once had a public banquet poem:
translations.idiomatic: At a feast he wrote:

sentences.zh: 」雖深於詩者，亦所歎伏。

translations.literal: "Before the curtain, pale clouds at the sun's edge; on the seat, dreary wind at the rain's foot."
translations.idiomatic: "Pale sun beyond the curtain; dreary rain-wind on the seat."

sentences.zh: 紹威子三人，長曰廷規，位至司農卿，尚太祖女安陽公主，又尚金華公主，早卒。

translations.literal: Even those deep in poetry sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Even masters of verse admired it.

sentences.zh: 次曰周翰，繼為魏博節度使，

translations.literal: Shaowei had three sons; the eldest Tinggui reached Minister of Agriculture, married the Founder's daughter Princess Anyang, also married Princess Jinhua, and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Tinggui became Minister of Agriculture, married two imperial princesses, and died young.

translations.literal: The second, Zhouhan, succeeded as Wei-Bo military commissioner,
translations.idiomatic: Second son Zhouhan succeeded as Wei commissioner,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒考異》引《梁功臣傳》云：周翰起復雲麾將軍，充天雄軍節度留後，尋檢校司徒，正授魏博節度使。）〉

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Zhouhan's succession:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Zhouhan's succession:

sentences.zh: 亦早卒。

translations.literal: (The 《Mirror Comprehensive Examined》 cites the 《Biographies of Liang Merit Ministers》: Zhouhan resumed office as Cloud Commander General, acting Tianxiong military commissioner, soon honorary Minister of Works, then formal Wei-Bo commissioner.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 supplement cites Zhouhan's rapid rise to Wei commissioner.)〉

sentences.zh: 季曰周敬，曆滑州節度使，別有傳。

translations.literal: He too died early.
translations.idiomatic: He too died young.

sentences.zh: 開平四年夏，詔金華公主出家為尼，居於宋州元靜寺，蓋太祖推恩於羅氏，令終其婦節也。

translations.literal: The youngest, Zhoujing, successively held Huazhou military commission; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Youngest son Zhoujing governed Huazhou and has his own biography.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Shaowei's comic judgments:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Shaowei's comic judgments:

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：羅鄴王紹威，俊邁有詞學，尤好戲判。

translations.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei was brilliant with literary learning and especially loved comic judgments.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Supplement》 says Shaowei loved comic judgments.)

sentences.zh: 常有人向官街中韝驢，置鞍於地，值牛車過，急行碾破其鞍，驢主怒，歐駕車者，為廂司所擒。

translations.literal: Once a man saddled a donkey in the official street, set the saddle on the ground, and an ox cart passing crushed the saddle in haste; the donkey owner in anger cursed the driver and was seized by gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: A donkey owner's saddle was crushed by a cart; he cursed the driver and was arrested.

sentences.zh: 紹威更不按問，遂判其狀云：「鄴城大道甚寬，何故駕車碾鞍？

translations.literal: Shaowei did not investigate further but judged the case: "The Ye city great road is very wide—why drive a cart to crush a saddle?"
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei judged without inquiry: "The road is wide—why crush his saddle?"

sentences.zh: 領韝驢漢子科決，待駕車漢子喜歡！

translations.literal: Punish the donkey man; wait until the cart driver is pleased!"
translations.idiomatic: Punish the donkey man—until the driver is happy!"

sentences.zh: 」詞雖俳諧，理甚切當，論者許之。）〉

translations.literal: Though the words were playful, the principle was very apt; discussers approved.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Playful words, sound justice—critics approved.)〉

sentences.zh: 趙犨，其先天水人。

translations.literal: Zhao Chou—his ancestors were Tianshui men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chou's family came from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 代為忠武牙將，曾祖賓，祖英奇，父叔文，皆曆故職。

translations.literal: For generations they were Zhongwu guard officers; great-grandfather Bin, grandfather Yingqi, father Shuwen—all held the old posts.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they served Zhongwu; Bin, Yingqi, and Shuwen held the family posts.

sentences.zh: 犨幼有奇智，齠齔之時，與鄰裏小兒戲於道左，恒分布行列為部伍戰陣之狀，自為董帥，指顧有節，如夙習焉，群兒皆稟而從之，無敢亂其行者。

translations.literal: Chou in youth had strange intelligence; in childhood playing with neighborhood boys on the road's left, he always arrayed ranks in battle formation, himself commander, directing with discipline as if long practiced; the boys all obeyed and none dared disorder his lines.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he drilled playmates in battle lines and commanded them like a veteran.

sentences.zh: 其父目而異之，曰：「吾家千里駒也，必大吾門矣！

translations.literal: His father looked and marveled, saying: "A thousand-li colt of our house—he will greatly enlarge our gate!"
translations.idiomatic: His father said, "A stallion of our house—you will enlarge our gate!"

sentences.zh: 」及赴鄉校，誦讀之性出於同輩。

translations.literal: When he went to district school, his nature for recitation surpassed his peers.
translations.idiomatic: At school he outread his peers.

sentences.zh: 弱冠有壯節，好功名，妙於弓劍，氣義勇果。

translations.literal: At weak cap he had strong integrity, loved fame and achievement, was skilled at bow and sword, righteous, brave, and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he sought glory, excelled at arms, and was bold and just.

sentences.zh: 郡守聞之，擢為牙校。

translations.literal: The prefect heard it and promoted him to guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect made him a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 唐會昌中，壺關作亂，隨父北征，收天井關。

translations.literal: In Huichang of Tang, Huguan rebelled; he followed his father north to campaign and recovered Tianjing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang he followed his father north and retook Tianjing Pass.

sentences.zh: 末幾，從王師征蠻，浹月方克，惟忠武將士轉戰溪洞之間，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Before long he followed the royal army against the southern tribes; after a full month they took them; only Zhongwu troops turned battle in stream caves and beheaded and captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in the south with the royal army; Zhongwu troops won heavy kills in the hill country.

sentences.zh: 本道錄其勳，陟為馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: The circuit recorded his merit and raised him to horse-and-foot chief commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit made him chief commandant of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，王仙芝起於曹、濮，大縱其徒，侵掠汝、鄭，犨乃率步騎數千襲之，賊黨南奔。

translations.literal: In Qianfu, Wang Xianzhi rose in Cao and Pu, greatly loosed his followers, and raided Ru and Zheng; Chou then led several thousand foot and horse to strike them and the bandits fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xianzhi raided Ru and Zheng, Chou drove him south with thousands of troops.

sentences.zh: 及黃巢陷長安，天子幸蜀，中原無主，人心騷動。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao took Chang'an, the Son of Heaven went to Shu; the Central Plain was masterless and hearts were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao took Chang'an and the emperor fled to Shu, the heartland panicked.

sentences.zh: 於是陳州數百人相率告許州連帥，願得犨知軍州事。

translations.literal: Then several hundred men of Chen prefecture together told the Xu circuit commander they wished Chou to govern the army and prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of Chen men asked the Xu commander to put Chou in charge.

sentences.zh: 其帥即以狀聞，於是天子下詔，以犨守陳州刺史。

translations.literal: The commander memorialized; the Son of Heaven issued an edict making Chou defend Chen as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him Chen prefect.

sentences.zh: 既視事，乃謂將吏曰：「賊巢之虐，遍於四方，苟不為長安市人所誅，則必驅殘黨以東下。

translations.literal: Once in office he told officers: "Bandit Chao's cruelty spreads in all directions; if not killed by Chang'an townspeople, he will surely drive remnant bands east.
translations.idiomatic: Taking office he warned, "If Chao is not killed in Chang'an he will drive east.

sentences.zh: 況與忠武久為仇讎，淩我土疆，勢必然也。

translations.literal: Moreover we have long been Zhongwu's enemies—they will trample our soil; the trend is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu hates us and will invade—that is certain."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣增垣墉，浚溝洫，實倉廩，積薪芻。

translations.literal: He then sent men to heighten walls, dredge moats, fill granaries, and pile fuel and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: He raised walls, dredged moats, and stocked grain and fodder.

sentences.zh: 凡四門之外，兩舍之內，民有資糧者，悉令挽入郡中。

translations.literal: Outside all four gates, within two houses' distance, people with grain and provisions were all ordered to haul into the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Within two li of the gates all grain was brought inside the city.

sentences.zh: 繕甲兵，利劍槊，弓弩矢石無不畢備。

translations.literal: He repaired armor and weapons, sharpened swords and spears; bows, crossbows, arrows, and stones were all fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: He armed the city with every weapon.

sentences.zh: 又招召勁勇，置之麾下。

translations.literal: He also recruited fierce braves and placed them under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited fierce men to his command.

sentences.zh: 以仲弟昶為防遏都指揮使，以季弟珝為親從都知兵馬使，長子麓、次子霖，皆分領銳兵。

translations.literal: He made his second brother Chang defense commander, his youngest brother Gui personal guard commander of horse and army; eldest son Lu and second son Lin each led crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers Chang and Gui commanded defense and guard; sons Lu and Lin led elite troops.

sentences.zh: 黃巢在長安，果為王師四面扼束，食盡人饑，謀東奔之計，先遣驍將孟楷擁徒萬人，直入項縣，犨引兵擊之。

translations.literal: Chao in Chang'an was indeed pinched by the royal army on four sides; food exhausted, men hungry, he planned to flee east, first sent fierce general Meng Kai with ten thousand followers straight into Xiang county; Chou led troops to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Starving in Chang'an, Chao sent Meng Kai east with ten thousand men; Chou attacked.

sentences.zh: 賊眾大潰，斬獲略盡，生擒孟楷。

translations.literal: The bandit masses were greatly routed; beheading and capture nearly complete; Meng Kai was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Chou routed the bandits and captured Meng Kai alive.

sentences.zh: 中和三年，朝廷聞其功，就加檢校兵部尚書，俄轉右僕射。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhonghe the court heard his merit and at once added honorary Minister of War; soon he was transferred to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe 3 the court made him honorary Minister of War, then Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 不數月，加司空，進潁川縣伯。

translations.literal: Within months he was made Grand Marshal and advanced to Earl of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Grand Marshal and Earl of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 巢黨知孟楷為陳所擒，大驚憤，乃悉眾東來，先據溵水，後與蔡州秦宗權合勢以攻宛丘，陳人懼焉。

translations.literal: Chao's party, learning Meng Kai was captured by Chen, were greatly shocked and angry; they then led all their masses east, first held Yin River, later joined Cai prefecture's Qin Zongquan to attack Wankiu; Chen people were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Meng Kai was taken, Chao marched east with Zongquan to besiege Chen; the city feared.

sentences.zh: 犨恐眾心攜離，乃於眾中揚言曰：「忠武素稱義勇，淮陽亦謂勁兵，是宜戮力同心，捍禦群寇，建功立節，去危就安，諸君宜圖之，況吾家食陳祿久矣！

translations.literal: Chou feared hearts would split and therefore proclaimed among the masses: "Zhongwu has always been called righteous and brave; Huaiyang too is said to have strong soldiers—you should join strength with one heart, defend against the band, achieve merit and establish honor, leave peril for safety—gentlemen should plan it; moreover our house has long eaten Chen's salary!"
translations.idiomatic: Fearing panic he rallied the men: "We have eaten Chen's pay—stand together, kill bandits, and win honor from peril!"

sentences.zh: 今賊眾圍逼，眾寡不均，男子當於死中求生，又何懼也。

translations.literal: Now bandits press the siege, few against many—men should seek life from death; what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: The enemy outnumbers us—seek life in death; what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 且死於為國，不猶愈於生而為賊之伍耶！

translations.literal: To die for the state is it not better than living in the bandits' ranks!"
translations.idiomatic: Dying for the state beats living with bandits!"

sentences.zh: 汝但觀吾之破賊，敢有異議者斬之！

translations.literal: Watch me break the bandits—whoever disagrees I behead!"
translations.idiomatic: Watch me break them—whoever wavers dies!"

sentences.zh: 」由是眾心靡不踴躍。

translations.literal: " From then the masses' hearts all leaped.
translations.idiomatic: The army's heart leaped to fight.

sentences.zh: 無何，開門與賊接戰，每戰皆捷，賊眾益怒。

translations.literal: Before long they opened the gates and met the bandits in battle; each battle was victorious; the bandit masses grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: They sallied and won every fight; the bandits raged.

sentences.zh: 巢於郡北三四里起八仙營，如宮闕之狀，又修百司廨署，儲蓄山峙，蔡人濟以甲胄，軍無所闕焉。

translations.literal: Chao north of the prefecture three or four li raised the Eight Immortals camp like palace halls, also repaired offices of the hundred bureaus, stores piled like mountains; Cai men supplied armor—nothing lacked in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Chao built a palace camp north of the city and stocked it like a capital with Cai armor.

sentences.zh: 凡圍陳三百日，大小數百戰，雖兵食將盡，然人心益固。

translations.literal: Altogether they besieged Chen three hundred days, great and small battles several hundred; though soldiers' food was nearly gone, the people's hearts grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: For three hundred days and hundreds of battles, starving Chen held firm.

sentences.zh: 犨因令間道奉羽書乞師於太祖，太祖素多犨之勇果，乃許之。

translations.literal: Chou therefore sent men by secret road with urgent letters begging troops from the Founder; the Founder had always valued Chou's courage and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Chou begged the Founder for aid by secret dispatch; the Founder agreed.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，太祖引大軍與諸軍會於陳之西北，陳人望旗鼓出軍縱火，急攻巢寨，賊眾大潰，重圍遂解。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of year 4 the Founder led a great army and united with other armies northwest of Chen; Chen people saw flags and drums, sallied with fire, urgently attacked Chao's camp; the bandit masses were greatly routed and the heavy siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Month 4, year 4, the Founder relieved Chen; the garrison sallied with fire and broke Chao's camp.

sentences.zh: 獻捷於行在。

translations.literal: Victory was presented at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Victory was reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 犨雖盡忠唐室，保全陳州，然默識太祖雄傑，每降心托跡，為子孫之計，故因解圍之後，以愛子結親。

translations.literal: Though Chou loyally served the Tang house and preserved Chen prefecture, he silently recognized the Founder's heroism, each time lowered his heart and attached his track for his sons' and grandsons' plan; therefore after the siege lifted he joined his beloved son in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal to Tang yet seeing the Founder's power, he married his son into the Founder's house after the siege.

sentences.zh: 又請為太祖立生祠於陳州，朝夕拜謁。

translations.literal: He also asked to erect a living shrine to the Founder at Chenzhou and worship morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: He built a living shrine to the Founder at Chen and worshipped daily.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，悉力委輸，凡所征調，無不率先，故能保其功名。

translations.literal: Within several years he exhausted strength in delivery; of all levies none was not first—thus he could preserve his fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: For years he supplied the Founder first in every levy and kept his fame.

sentences.zh: 昶，字大東，犨仲弟也。

translations.literal: Chang, style name Dadong, was Chou's second brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, styled Dadong, was Chou's second brother.

sentences.zh: 弱冠習兵機，沈默大度，神形灑落，臨事有通變之才。

translations.literal: At weak cap he studied military arts, was silent and magnanimous, spirit and form free and easy, and in affairs had talent for flexible response.
translations.idiomatic: Young he mastered warfare, was calm and broad, and handled crises with ease.

sentences.zh: 及兄犨為陳州刺史，以昶為防禦都指揮使。

translations.literal: When elder brother Chou was Chen prefect, he made Chang defense commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou governed Chen he made Chang defense commander.

sentences.zh: 未幾，巢將孟楷擁眾萬餘據項城縣，昶與兄犨領兵擊破之，擒楷以歸。

translations.literal: Before long Chao's general Meng Kai held Xiangcheng county with more than ten thousand; Chang and brother Chou led troops, defeated them, and captured Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He and Chou defeated Meng Kai at Xiangcheng and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 不數月，巢黨悉眾攻陳，以報孟楷之役；

translations.literal: Within months Chao's party led all their masses to attack Chen to avenge Meng Kai;
translations.idiomatic: Months later Chao's whole host besieged Chen to avenge Kai;

sentences.zh: 又與蔡寇合從，凶醜百萬，棲於陳郊，陳人大恐。

translations.literal: They also joined Cai bandits; ferocious villains a million encamped on Chen's outskirts; Chen people were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: A million bandits with Cai allies camped at Chen's walls.

sentences.zh: 一夕，昶因巡警，假寐於闍，恍惚間如有陰助，昶異而待之。

translations.literal: One night Chang while on patrol dozed at the gate; in a trance it was as if there were hidden aid; Chang marveled and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Patrolling one night he dozed at the gate and felt unseen aid.

sentences.zh: 遲明，開門決戰，人心兵勢，勇不可遏，若有陰兵前導。

translations.literal: At dawn he opened the gates for decisive battle; soldiers' hearts and martial momentum could not be checked—as if yin troops led the way.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he charged as if ghost soldiers led.

sentences.zh: 是日，擒賊將數人，斬首千餘級，群凶氣沮。

translations.literal: That day they captured several bandit generals and beheaded more than a thousand; the vicious masses' spirit was damped.
translations.idiomatic: That day he took bandit generals and a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 其後連日交戰，無不應機俘斬，未嘗小衄，以至重圍數月，士心如一。

translations.literal: Afterward daily battles met the moment in capture and beheading, never a small setback, until the heavy siege of months with soldiers' hearts as one.
translations.idiomatic: Daily victories followed until months of siege left the army united.

sentences.zh: 及賊敗圍解，朝廷紀勳，昶一門之中，疊加爵秩。

translations.literal: When the bandits were defeated and the siege lifted, the court recorded merit; Chang's whole household received stacked ranks.
translations.idiomatic: After relief the court heaped honors on Chang's house.

sentences.zh: 當時方鎮之內，言忠勇者、言守禦者、言功勳者、言政事者，皆以犨、昶為首焉。

translations.literal: Among frontier governors then, for loyal courage, for defense, for achievement, for government—all spoke of Chou and Chang first.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier lords ranked Chou and Chang first in loyalty, defense, merit, and rule.

sentences.zh: 及犨遙領泰寧軍節度，以昶為本州刺史、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: When Chou held Taining military commission at a distance, he made Chang this prefecture's prefect and honorary Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Chou made Chang Taizhou prefect and honorary Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 俄而犨有疾，遂以軍州盡付於昶。

translations.literal: Soon Chou fell ill and entrusted army and prefecture entirely to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, Chou gave army and prefecture to Chang.

sentences.zh: 詔授兵馬留後，旋遷忠武軍節度使，亦以陳州為理所。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him army and horse acting commissioner; soon he was transferred Zhongwu military commissioner, also taking Chen as seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: He became acting commissioner, then Zhongwu commissioner with Chen as capital.

sentences.zh: 時宗權未滅，中原方受其毒。

translations.literal: At that time Zongquan was not yet destroyed and the Central Plain still suffered his poison.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan still poisoned the heartland.

sentences.zh: 陳、蔡封疆相接，昶每選精銳，深入蔡境。

translations.literal: Chen and Cai borders adjoined; Chang each time chose crack troops and penetrated deep into Cai territory.
translations.idiomatic: Chang raided deep into Cai from neighboring Chen.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊雖眾，終不能抗，以至宗權敗焉。

translations.literal: Though Cai bandits were many, in the end they could not resist, until Zongquan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Cai could not stand against him until Zongquan fell.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賞勳，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: The court rewarded merit and added honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The court made him honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 昶以大寇削平之後，益留心於政事，勸課農桑，大布恩惠。

translations.literal: After the great bandit was cut down, Chang gave his heart more to government affairs, urged farming and mulberry, and broadly spread grace.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he promoted farming and generous rule.

sentences.zh: 景福元年秋，陳、許將吏耆老錄其功，詣闕以聞，天子嘉之，命文臥撰德政碑植於通衢，以旌其功。

translations.literal: In autumn of Jingfu year 1, Chen and Xu officers and elders recorded his merit and went to court; the Son of Heaven praised it and ordered Wen Wo to compose a virtue monument planted at the crossroads to display his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfu 1 the court erected Wen Wo's virtue stele for Chang at the crossroads.

sentences.zh: 俄加同平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 昶自圍解之後，恒曰：「梁王之恩，不敢忘也。

translations.literal: After the siege lifted Chang always said: "Prince of Liang's grace—I dare not forget."
translations.idiomatic: After the siege he said, "I dare not forget the Prince of Liang."

sentences.zh: 」是後太祖每有征伐，昶訓練兵甲，饋挽供億，無有不至。

translations.literal: Afterward whenever the Founder campaigned, Chang trained armor and weapons and supplied transport—nothing failed to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Founder marched, Chang supplied men and grain.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年寢疾，薨於鎮，年五十五，追贈太尉。

translations.literal: In Qianning year 2 he fell ill in bed and died in his post at age fifty-five; posthumously he was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianning 2 at fifty-five and was posthumously named Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 珝，字有節，犨季弟也。

translations.literal: Gui, style name Youjie, was Chou's youngest brother.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, styled Youjie, was Chou's youngest brother.

sentences.zh: 幼而剛毅，器宇深沉。

translations.literal: In youth he was firm and resolute; bearing and capacity were deep and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful, firm and deep in bearing.

sentences.zh: 既冠，好書籍。

translations.literal: Once capped, he loved books.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he loved books.

sentences.zh: 及壯，工騎射，尤精《三略》。

translations.literal: When grown, he was skilled at mounted archery and especially refined in the 《Three Strategies》.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he excelled at archery and the 《Three Strategies》.

sentences.zh: 及犨為陳州刺史，以珝為親從都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Chou was Chen prefect, he made Gui personal guard commander of horse and army.
translations.idiomatic: Chou made him personal guard commander.

sentences.zh: 時巢黨東出商、鄧，與蔡賊會，眾至百餘萬，掘長壕五百道攻陳，陳人大懼。

translations.literal: At that time Chao's party went east through Shang and Deng, joined Cai bandits, masses reached more than a million, dug long trenches five hundred routes to attack Chen; Chen people were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's millions with Cai allies dug five hundred trench lines around Chen.

sentences.zh: 珝與二兄堅心誓眾，激勵將校，約以死節。

translations.literal: Gui with his two brothers steeled hearts and swore the masses, roused officers, and pledged death with honor.
translations.idiomatic: The three brothers swore the army to die defending Chen.

sentences.zh: 珝以祖先鬆楸，去郭數里，慮為群盜穿發，乃夜縱心膂之士，遷柩入城。

translations.literal: Gui, because ancestral pine and oak tombs were several li outside the wall, feared bandits would violate them, and by night led trusted men to move the coffins into the city.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the family tombs inside the walls lest bandits violate them.

sentences.zh: 府庫舊有巨弩數百枝，機牙皆缺，工人咸謂不可用。

translations.literal: In the government store were several hundred great crossbows whose mechanisms were all broken; craftsmen all said they could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of great crossbows in store were broken; craftsmen said they were useless.

sentences.zh: 珝即創意制度，自調弦筈，置之雉堞間，矢激五百餘步，凡中人馬，皆洞達胸腋，群賊畏之，不敢逼近。

translations.literal: Gui then devised a new design, himself adjusted strings and notches, set them on the battlements; arrows reached more than five hundred paces; all who hit men or horses were pierced through chest and flank; the bandits feared and did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: Gui rebuilt them; bolts pierced men five hundred paces off and kept bandits at bay.

sentences.zh: 自仲秋至於首夏，軍食將竭，士雖不飽，而堅拒之志不移。

translations.literal: From mid-autumn to first summer, army food was nearly gone; though soldiers were not full, the will to hold fast did not shift.
translations.idiomatic: From autumn to summer they starved yet never broke.

sentences.zh: 會太祖率大軍解其圍，珝兄弟抆泣感謝。

translations.literal: When the Founder led a great army to lift the siege, the Gui brothers wiped tears in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder relieved the siege the brothers wept thanks.

sentences.zh: 其後朝廷議功，加檢校右僕射，遙領處州刺史。

translations.literal: Afterward the court discussed merit and added honorary Right Vice Director, holding Chuzhou military commission at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored him Right Vice Director and distant Chuzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 犨薨，昶為忠武軍節度使，珝遷為行軍司馬、檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Chou died, Chang was Zhongwu military commissioner; Gui was transferred to campaign deputy and honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: After Chou's death Gui became campaign deputy under Chang.

sentences.zh: 昶薨，珝知忠武軍留後。

translations.literal: When Chang died, Gui knew Zhongwu military affairs as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang died Gui acted as Zhongwu commissioner.

sentences.zh: 珝公幹之才，播於遠邇，至於符籍虛實，財穀耗登，備閱其根本，民之利病，無不洞知。

translations.literal: Gui's public talent was broadcast far and near; registers of tallies, granary reality, wealth and grain intake and expenditure—he had reviewed the roots; the people's benefit and harm—nothing was not thoroughly known.
translations.idiomatic: He knew every register, granary, and hardship of the people.

sentences.zh: 庶事簡廉，公私俱濟，太祖深加慰薦。

translations.literal: Common affairs were simple and clean; public and private both aided; the Founder deeply comforted and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: His clean rule won the Founder's praise.

sentences.zh: 尋加特進、檢校司徒，充忠武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was specially advanced and made honorary Minister of Works, full Zhongwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Grand Marshal and full Zhongwu commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陳州土壤卑疏，每歲壁壘摧圮，工役不暇，珝遂營度力用，俾以甓周砌四墉，自是無霖潦之虞。

translations.literal: Chenzhou's soil was low and loose; each year walls and ramparts collapsed and labor never ceased; Gui then planned strength and use, had brick circle the four walls, and from then was without fear of rain flood.
translations.idiomatic: He bricked Chen's crumbling walls against flood.

sentences.zh: 光化二年，加檢校太保、平章事。

translations.literal: In Guanghua year 2 he was made honorary Grand Guardian and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghua 2 he became Grand Guardian and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 明年，檢校侍中，進封天水郡公。

translations.literal: The next year, honorary Palace Secretary, advanced to Duke of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he was Palace Secretary and Duke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 珝博通前古，以陳州本伏羲所都，南頓乃光武舊地，遂稽考古制，崇飾廟貌，為四民祈福之所。

translations.literal: Gui was broadly versed in antiquity; because Chenzhou was originally Fuxi's capital and Nandun was Emperor Guangwu's old ground, he examined ancient systems and honored temple appearances as a place for the four peoples to pray for blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Fuxi and Guangwu shrines at Chen for public worship.

sentences.zh: 又詢鄧艾故址，決翟王河以溉稻粱，大實倉廩，民獲其利。

translations.literal: He also sought Deng Ai's old site, opened the Zhaiwang River to irrigate rice and millet, greatly filled granaries, and the people received the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Zhaiwang River on Deng Ai's route and filled the granaries.

sentences.zh: 珝兄弟節制陳、許，繼擁旌鉞，共二十餘年，陳人愛戴，風化大行。

translations.literal: The Gui brothers controlled Chen and Xu, successively held banners and axes more than twenty years; Chen people loved and supported them and transforming instruction was greatly practiced.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years the Zhao brothers ruled Chen and Xu and won the people's love.

sentences.zh: 天復元年冬，韓建為忠武軍節度使，乃征珝知同州匡國軍節度留後。

translations.literal: In winter of Tianfu year 1, Han Jian was Zhongwu military commissioner; he then summoned Gui to know Tongzhou Kuangguo military affairs as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 1 winter Han Jian summoned Gui to Tongzhou as acting Kuangguo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時太祖統軍岐下，珝輸挽調發，旁午道途。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder commanded troops below Qi; Gui's transport and levies crowded the roads.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder campaigned at Qi, Gui fed the armies on the roads.

sentences.zh: 俄而昭宗還長安，詔征入覲，錫迎鑾功臣之號。

translations.literal: Soon Zhaozong returned to Chang'an; an edict summoned him to audience and granted the title Merit Minister Welcoming the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Chang'an, Gui was summoned and honored as Welcoming-the-Carriage merit minister.

sentences.zh: 珝因堅辭藩鎮，遂加檢校太傅、右金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Gui firmly declined frontier command and was then made honorary Grand Tutor and Right Golden Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Declining the frontier, he became Grand Tutor and Golden Guard general.

sentences.zh: 及扈從東遷，歲餘，以痼疾免官，遂歸淮陽。

translations.literal: When escorting the move east, after more than a year he was released from office for chronic illness and returned to Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the court east, he retired ill to Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，薨於私第，年五十五。

translations.literal: Before long he died at his private residence at age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 詔贈侍中，陳人為之罷市。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Palace Secretary; Chen people closed the markets for him.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Palace Secretary; Chen closed its markets in mourning.

sentences.zh: 子縠，仕至左驍衛大將軍、宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: His son Gu rose to Left Valiant Cavalry great general and Proclamation commissioner of the northern palace bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Son Gu became Left Valiant Cavalry general and northern palace commissioner.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗入汴，與從兄岩皆族誅。

translations.literal: When Later Tang Zhuangzong entered Bian, he and cousin Yan were both clan-executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took Bian, he and cousin Yan were executed with their clans.

sentences.zh: 王珂，河中人。

translations.literal: Wang Ke was a Hedong man.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖縱，鹽州刺史。

translations.literal: Grandfather Zong was Yan prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zong was Yan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 父重榮，河東節度使，破黃巢有大功，封琅邪郡王。

translations.literal: Father Chongrong was Hedong military commissioner; he broke Huang Chao with great merit and was enfeoffed Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chongrong, Hedong commissioner, broke Huang Chao and became Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 珂本重榮兄重簡之子，出繼重榮。

translations.literal: Ke was originally son of Chongrong's elder brother Chongjian and was given in adoption to Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was Chongjian's son, adopted by Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 唐僖宗光啟三年，重榮為部將常行儒所害，推重榮弟重盈為蒲帥，以珂為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangqi of Tang Xizong, Chongrong was killed by his officer Chang Xingru; they pushed Chongrong's younger brother Chongying as Pu commander and made Ke campaign deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi 3 Chongrong was killed; Chongying took Pu and made Ke deputy.

sentences.zh: 及重盈卒，軍府推珂為留後。

translations.literal: When Chongying died, the military government pushed Ke to be acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongying died the army made Ke acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時重盈子珙為陝州節度使，瑤為絳州刺史，由是爭為蒲帥，瑤、珙連上章論列，又與太祖書云：「珂非吾兄弟，蓋餘家之蒼頭也，小字忠兒，安得繼嗣！

translations.literal: At that time Chongying's son Gong was Shan military commissioner and Yao was Jiang prefect; therefore they contended for Pu command; Yao and Gong repeatedly memorialized and also wrote the Founder: "Ke is not our brother—he is another family's house slave, pet name Zhong'er—how can he succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Cousins Gong and Yao disputed the succession, calling Ke a household slave unfit to rule.

sentences.zh: 」珂亦上章云：「亡父有興復之功。

translations.literal: Ke also memorialized: "My dead father had merit in restoration."
translations.idiomatic: Ke memorialized that his father had restored the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」又遣使求援於太原，李克用為保薦於朝，昭宗可之。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys seeking aid from Taiyuan; Li Keyong memorialized support at court and Zhaozong approved.
translations.idiomatic: He begged Taiyuan; Keyong backed him and Zhaozong agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而珙厚結王行瑜、李茂貞、韓建為援，三鎮互相表薦，昭宗詔諭之曰：「吾以太原與重榮有再造之功，已俞其奏矣。

translations.literal: Soon Gong thickly joined Wang Xingyu, Li Maozhen, and Han Jian as aid; the three circuits mutually memorialized recommendation; Zhaozong edicted them: "I grant Taiyuan's memorial because of renewal merit with Chongrong."
translations.idiomatic: Gong won Wang Xingyu, Maozhen, and Han Jian; the court favored Ke for Chongrong's service to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 」乾寧二年五月，三鎮率兵入覲，賊害時政，請以河中授珙、瑤，又連兵以攻河中。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Qianning year 2 the three circuits led troops to audience, harmed current politics, and asked that Hezhong be given to Gong and Yao; they also united troops to attack Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Qianning 2, month 5, the three circuits marched on court politics and attacked Hezhong for Gong and Yao.

sentences.zh: 克用聞之，出師以討三鎮，瑤、珙兵退，晉師拔絳州，擒瑤斬之。

translations.literal: Keyong heard it and led troops to attack the three circuits; Yao and Gong's troops withdrew; Jin troops took Jiang prefecture and captured and beheaded Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong drove them off and beheaded Yao at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及克用駐軍於渭北，昭宗以珂為河中節度使，正授旄鉞，克用因以女妻珂；

translations.literal: When Keyong camped north of Wei, Zhaozong made Ke Hezhong military commissioner, formally granted axe and banner; Keyong therefore gave his daughter to Ke in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong camped at Wei; the court confirmed Ke at Hezhong and Keyong gave him his daughter;

sentences.zh: 珂至太原謝婚成禮，克用令李嗣昭將兵助珂，攻珙於陝焉。

translations.literal: Ke reached Taiyuan to thank for the marriage rites; Keyong ordered Li Sizhao to lead troops to aid Ke and attack Gong at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Ke married at Taiyuan; Keyong sent Li Sizhao against Gong at Shan.

sentences.zh: 光化末，太祖謂張存敬曰：「珂恃太原之勢，侮慢鄰封，爾為我持一繩以縛之。

translations.literal: At the end of Guanghua the Founder told Zhang Cunjing: "Ke relies on Taiyuan's power and insults neighboring circuits—you hold one rope and bind him for me."
translations.idiomatic: Late in Guanghua the Founder told Zhang Cunjing to bind Ke with a rope.

sentences.zh: 」天復元年春，存敬兵下晉、絳，令何糸因守晉州以扼太原援師。

translations.literal: In spring of Tianfu year 1 Cunjing's troops descended on Jin and Jiang and ordered He Yinsi to hold Jin prefecture to choke Taiyuan relief.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 1 spring Cunjing seized Jin and Jiang and blocked Taiyuan relief at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，大軍逼河中，珂妻書告太原曰：「敵勢攻逼，朝夕為俘囚，乞食於大梁矣，大人安忍不救！

translations.literal: In the second month the great army pressed Hezhong; Ke's wife wrote Taiyuan: "The enemy presses hard; soon captive— I beg food at Daliang; how can you bear not to save!"
translations.idiomatic: Besieged, Ke's wife wrote Keyong, "We will be prisoners unless you save us from Daliang!"

sentences.zh: 」克用曰：「前途既阻，眾寡不敵，救則與爾兩亡。

translations.literal: Keyong said: "The road ahead is blocked, few against many—if we rescue, we perish together with you.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong said, "The road is blocked—we would die together."

sentences.zh: 可與王郎歸朝廷。

translations.literal: You may with Prince Wang return to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Go to the court with Prince Wang."

sentences.zh: 」珂復求救於李茂貞，茂貞不答。

translations.literal: Ke again begged rescue from Li Maozhen; Maozhen did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Ke begged Maozhen, who refused.

sentences.zh: 珂勢窮蹙，即登城謂存敬曰：「吾與汴王有家世事分，公宜退舍，俟汴王至，吾自聽命。

translations.literal: Ke in desperate straits ascended the wall and told Cunjing: "I and Prince of Liang have family affair from old—sir should withdraw camp and wait until Prince of Liang arrives—I myself will obey."
translations.idiomatic: Ke called down, "I am kin to the Prince of Liang—withdraw until he comes."

sentences.zh: 」存敬即日退舍。

translations.literal: Cunjing that day withdrew camp.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing withdrew that day.

sentences.zh: 三月，太祖自洛陽至，先哭於重榮之墓，蒲人聞之感悅。

translations.literal: In the third month the Founder came from Luoyang, first wept at Chongrong's tomb; Pu people heard and were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Month 3 the Founder came from Luoyang and wept at Chongrong's tomb; Pu was moved.

sentences.zh: 珂欲麵縛牽羊以見，太祖曰：「太師阿舅之恩，何時可忘，郎君若以亡國之禮相見，黃泉其謂我何！」

translations.literal: Ke wished to present himself bound with sheep in leading rope to meet; the Founder said: "Grand Marshal maternal-uncle's grace—when can it be forgotten! If you, sir, meet me with a lost-state rite, the yellow springs will say what of me!"
translations.idiomatic: Ke offered to surrender bound with a sheep; the Founder refused, citing Chongrong's kindness.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on the Founder and Chongrong as kin:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on the Founder and Chongrong as kin:

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》云：梁太祖自同州降唐，即依重榮，以母王氏，故事重榮為舅。）〉

translations.literal: (Ouyang Xiu's 《Historical Records》 says: Liang Founder from Tongzhou submitted to Tang and relied on Chongrong; because his mother was Lady Wang, by custom Chongrong was maternal uncle.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang Xiu notes the Founder called Chongrong uncle through Lady Wang.)〉

sentences.zh: 及珂出迎於路，握手歔欷，聯轡而入。

translations.literal: When Ke came out to welcome on the road, they clasped hands and sobbed and entered reins linked.
translations.idiomatic: Ke met him on the road; they wept and entered together.

sentences.zh: 乃以居敬守河中，珂舉家徙於汴。

translations.literal: He then had Jujing guard Hezhong; Ke moved his whole household to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Jujing held Hezhong; Ke moved his family to Bian.

sentences.zh: 後入覲，被殺於華州傳舍。

translations.literal: Later he entered audience and was killed at Huazhou relay lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Later at audience he was killed at a Huazhou inn.

sentences.zh: 珙，少有俊氣，才兼文武，性甚驕虐。

translations.literal: Gong in youth had handsome spirit; talent combined civil and military; nature was very arrogant and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was talented yet arrogant and cruel.

sentences.zh: 屬世多故，遂代伯父重霸為陝州節度使。

translations.literal: The age had many troubles; he then replaced his uncle Chongba as Shan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In troubled times he replaced uncle Chongba at Shan.

sentences.zh: 為政苛暴，且多猜忌，殘忍好殺，不以生命為意，內至妻孥宗屬，外則賓幕將吏，一言不合，則五毒將施，鞭笞刳斮，無日無之。

translations.literal: His government was harsh and violent and much suspicious; cruel and fond of killing, he did not take life as a thing—within to wives, children, and clan, outside to guests, staff, and officers—one word not fitting and the five punishments were applied; flogging, slicing, and cutting—no day without them.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with torture and suspicion, killing kin and staff on a whim daily.

sentences.zh: 奢縱聚斂，民不堪命，由是左右惕懼，憂在不測。

translations.literal: Extravagant, willful, and gathering wealth—the people could not bear the mandate; therefore left and right were fearful, worry in uncertainty.
translations.idiomatic: His greed and cruelty made everyone fear for their lives.

sentences.zh: 唐光化二年夏六月，為部將李璠所殺。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer of Guanghua year 2 of Tang, he was killed by his officer Li Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghua 2, month 6, officer Li Fan killed him.

sentences.zh: 璠自稱留後，因是陝州不復為王氏所有。

translations.literal: Fan declared himself acting commissioner; from then Shan no longer belonged to the Wang house.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan seized Shan and ended Wang rule there.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：紹威始為唐雄，據魏地，當土德之季運，倡梁祖以強禪，在梁則為佐命也，在唐則豈得為忠臣乎！

translations.literal: The historian says: Shaowei at first was a Tang hero, held Wei land, at earth virtue's declining fortune urged Liang Founder to strong abdication—in Liang he was aide in mandate; in Tang could he be called a loyal minister?
translations.idiomatic: The historian asks: Shaowei aided Liang's usurpation—hero to Liang, traitor to Tang?

sentences.zh: 趙犨以淮陽咫尺之地，抗黃巢百萬之眾，功成事立，有足多者。

translations.literal: Zhao Chou with Huaiyang land a stone's throw wide resisted Huang Chao's million masses—merit achieved, affair established—there is much to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chou held tiny Chen against Chao's millions—his defense deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 岩、縠非賢，遽泯其嗣，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yan and Gu were not worthy; soon their line was extinguished—pity!
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy Yan and Gu ended the line—pity!

sentences.zh: 王珂奕世山河，勢危被擄，乃魏豹之徒與！

translations.literal: Wang Ke for generations held mountains and rivers, in peril was captured—he was of Wei Bao's kind!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke lost his hereditary domain like Wei Bao!
